verdict: Two real failures: one test bug (wrong month in the fixed clock) and one likely product bug (out-of-stock sizes stay enabled); two localhost page.goto timeouts that passed on retry.

failures.test: Delivery estimate › the delivery date range is calculated from the visitor's date after load
failures.summary: The test sets the clock to November 5 because JS months are 0-indexed, so the page correctly shows a November range instead of 'Oct 08-12'.
failures.evidence: Source line 10: `new Date(2026, 10, 5, 10)` (month 10 = November) vs comment 'Monday 5 October 2026'; snapshot shows `definition: Nov 10-12`, which is 3–5 working days after Thu 5 Nov.
failures.next_step: Change line 10 to `new Date(2026, 9, 5, 10)` so the date is 5 October, then rerun and confirm 'Oct 08-12' appears.

failures.test: Product info › sizes that are out of stock for the colour are disabled
failures.summary: With Mustard selected, the S and XL size radios are labelled out of stock but are not disabled.
failures.evidence: `Expected: disabled / Received: enabled`; snapshot shows `radio "S (out of stock)"` and `radio "XL (out of stock)"` with no [disabled] state.
failures.next_step: Check the variant picker code that adds the '(out of stock)' label and confirm it also sets `disabled` on the size input; if leaving these sizes selectable is intended, update the test instead.

failures.test: Product info › quantity cannot go above the stock of the selected variant
failures.summary: The beforeEach navigation to localhost timed out waiting for the load event, and the test passed on retry.
failures.evidence: `TimeoutError: page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded ... waiting until "load"`; outcome flaky, attempts 2.
failures.next_step: Look for a slow subresource that delays the load event on the local server, or have gotoProduct wait for 'domcontentloaded' and then assert on the product heading.

failures.test: Product info › Add to Cart updates the header basket badge
failures.summary: Same beforeEach page.goto load timeout as the quantity test; the page had rendered but the load event never fired, and the test passed on retry.
failures.evidence: `TimeoutError: page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`; the snapshot shows the full product page with 'Calculating delivery date' still pending, status 200.
failures.next_step: Investigate with the quantity-test timeout: run both specs with tracing on and find which request holds back the load event.
